identity.title: Radio Jet Feedback and Star Formation in Heavily Obscured, Hyperluminous Quasars at Redshifts ∼ 0.5-3. I. ALMA Observations

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA 870 $\mu$m (345 GHz) data for 49 high redshift (0.47$<z<$2.85), luminous ($11.7<\log (L_{\rm bol}/L_{\odot})<14.2$) radio-powerful AGN

targets.name: 49 WISE-NVSS radio-powerful obscured quasars (southern subsample of 156)

evidence.quote: The declination range for the ALMA subsample was chosen to allow access to many northern facilities as well as ALMA: $-40^{\circ}<{\delta}<$+1$^{\circ}$.

question.value: How much cool dust emission / star formation accompanies highly obscured, radio-powerful WISE-selected quasars at z~0.5-3, as measured with ALMA 870 um snapshot photometry?

evidence.quote: obtained to constrain cool dust emission from starbursts concurrent with highly obscured radiative-mode black hole (BH) accretion in massive galaxies which possess a small radio jet.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00397.S.
The central frequency was set to 345 GHz (870 $\mu$m), with an 8 GHz bandwidth split into two sidebands.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: TDM, 256 channels per sideband, 14 km/s resolution

evidence.quote: The objects were observed with the correlator in Time Division Mode, which results in 256 channels per sideband with a spectral resolution of 14 km s$^{-1}$.
Fifteen antennas were used in the “compact” Early Science configuration for the November 2011 observations, 19 for the May 2012 observations and 23 for the August observations.
The resulting beamsizes are 1$\ensuremath{''}$2, 0$\ensuremath{''}$5 and 1$\ensuremath{''}$2, respectively.
Time on source was 1.5 min per object, resulting in an $rms$ noise of 0.3–0.6 mJy
Time on source was 1.5 min per object
Twenty-three sources were observed with ALMA in two Band 7 scheduling blocks on 2011 November 16. An additional 14 were observed on 2012 May 25 and the final 12 on 2012 August 29.

provided.value: 3.4-22 um photometry for selection and SEDs

evidence.quote: we cross-matched the NVSS catalog, which covers the sky north of ${\delta}=-40^{\circ}$, with point sources from the WISE Allsky Catalog.

evidence.quote: PACS observations are available for two sources, W1500-0649 and W2059-3541, and SPIRE observations for one, W2059-3541.
Two additional sources have upper limits from the CSO at 350$\mu$m, W1343-1136 and W1400-2919.

method.value: imfit in CASA on ALMA images; 26 detections at >=3 sigma, none resolved

evidence.quote: There are 26 ALMA detections at 3$\sigma$ or above. None of the sources are resolved.

We derive ISM masses (Table [5](#tbl-mass), columns 13 & 14), for dust temperatures of 30 K and 90 K

assumptions.value: uncertainty factor of 5; synchrotron contamination not corrected

evidence.quote: We estimate the overall uncertainty to be a factor of 5

evidence.quote: Their “IR Bright” sample has a median ISM mass of 11.91$\pm$0.77 ${\times} 10^{10} M_{\odot}$, about twice that of our sample.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit SEDs (AGN torus + modified blackbody + stellar) and derive SFRs

method.value: parametric AGN MIR component plus greybody at fixed T=30,50,90,120 K, beta=1.5 (2 for 50 K); SFR from Kennicutt conversion

evidence.quote: We have made four fits to each source, each with a different temperature for the BB component.
For $\beta$ we have selected a value of 1.5
For the four sources without measured redshift we assume $z = 2$.

validation.value: free-Td fits for two Herschel sources set 90 K and 120 K

evidence.quote: we have adopted the two dust temperature values which have fitted W1500-0649 and W2059-3541 successfully: 90 K (rounding up from 89 K) and 120 K

evidence.quote: We use a standard $\chi^2$ minimization technique to find the model parameters that best fit the data.

findings_qualitative.value: MIR-submm SEDs are similar to radio-blind Hot DOGs and redder than Spitzer DOGs, AGN-dominated in MIR

evidence.quote: They are redder in the NIR-MIR than previous samples selected from $Spitzer$ surveys, including almost all of the $Spitzer$ DOGs.

claims.hypothesis: Are obscured radio-powerful WISE quasars dominated by AGN with limited star formation?
claims.experiment: ALMA 870 um photometry plus SED modelling
claims.result: Large MIR/submm ratios; SFR from hundreds to thousands Msun/yr possible but AGN-only fits also possible
claims.finding: Sources are AGN-dominated, with star formation uncertain and dependent on dust temperature

evidence.quote: however we cannot rule out the alternative that the AGN powers all the emission in some cases.

claims.hypothesis: Does the best-constrained source host a starburst?
claims.result: comparable AGN and starburst luminosity, starburst age 10-15 Myr
claims.finding: Young compact starburst contributes about half of luminosity

evidence.quote: Our best constrained source has radiative transfer solutions with $\sim$ equal contributions for an obscured AGN and a young (10–15 Myr) compact starburst.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Synchrotron contribution to 345 GHz flux judged <10% for most steep-spectrum sources; blazar explanation rejected

evidence.loc: 4.3 Synchrotron Contribution to the ALMA fluxes
evidence.quote: None of the flat or inverted spectrum sources has a plausible SED that can explain the WISE data as synchrotron emission from a blazar.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust temperature unconstrained for most sources; L_BB and SFR uncertain by orders of magnitude

evidence.quote: is uncertain by 2-3 dex without measurements at the FIR peak of the dust SED.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single ALMA point beyond 22 um makes SFR highly degenerate with dust temperature
Snapshot data unresolved; AGN heating of cool dust not separable
Eddington ratio and covering factor assumptions drive BH masses
